verses.text: David again gathered together all the chosen men of Israel, thirty thousand.

David arose, and went with all the people who were with him, from Baale Judah, to bring up from there God’s ark, which is called by the Name, even the name of Yahweh of Armies who sits above the cherubim.
They set God’s ark on a new cart, and brought it out of Abinadab’s house that was on the hill; and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drove the new cart.
They brought it out of Abinadab’s house, which was in the hill, with God’s ark; and Ahio went before the ark.
David and all the house of Israel played before Yahweh with all kinds of instruments made of cypress wood, with harps, with stringed instruments, with tambourines, with castanets, and with cymbals.
When they came to the threshing floor of Nacon, Uzzah reached for God’s ark, and took hold of it; for the cattle stumbled.
Yahweh’s anger burned against Uzzah; and God struck him there for his error; and he died there by God’s ark.
David was displeased, because Yahweh had broken out against Uzzah; and he called that place Perez Uzzah,  to this day.
David was afraid of Yahweh that day; and he said, “How could Yahweh’s ark come to me?”
So David would not move Yahweh’s ark to be with him in David’s city; but David carried it aside into Obed-Edom the Gittite’s house.
Yahweh’s ark remained in Obed-Edom the Gittite’s house three months; and Yahweh blessed Obed-Edom and all his house.

King David was told, “Yahweh has blessed the house of Obed-Edom, and all that belongs to him, because of God’s ark.” So David went and brought up God’s ark from the house of Obed-Edom into David’s city with joy.
When those who bore Yahweh’s ark had gone six paces, he sacrificed an ox and a fattened calf.
David danced before Yahweh with all his might; and David was clothed in a linen ephod.
So David and all the house of Israel brought up Yahweh’s ark with shouting, and with the sound of the trumpet.
As Yahweh’s ark came into David’s city, Michal the daughter of Saul looked out through the window, and saw king David leaping and dancing before Yahweh; and she despised him in her heart.
They brought in Yahweh’s ark, and set it in its place, in the middle of the tent that David had pitched for it; and David offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before Yahweh.
When David had finished offering the burnt offering and the peace offerings, he blessed the people in the name of Yahweh of Armies.
He gave to all the people, even among the whole multitude of Israel, both to men and women, to everyone a portion of bread, dates, and raisins. So all the people departed, each to his own house.

Then David returned to bless his household. Michal the daughter of Saul came out to meet David, and said, “How glorious the king of Israel was today, who uncovered himself today in the eyes of the servants of his servants, as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovers himself!”

David said to Michal, “It was before Yahweh, who chose me above your father, and above all his house, to appoint me prince over the people of Yahweh, over Israel. Therefore I will celebrate before Yahweh.
I will be yet more vile than this, and will be base in my own sight. But of the servants of whom you have spoken, they will honor me.”
Michal the daughter of Saul had no child to the day of her death.

footnotes.content: Thirty thousand—such a throng! David's heart has turned toward the Lord, and he gathers strength to do what's been left undone. Sometimes it takes a while for us to find our courage; the good thing is, grace doesn't charge interest for the delay.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He goes to Baale Judah to fetch the ark—the seat of Yahweh of Armies. Notice that David is moving toward the Lord with purpose and full attendance. When we finally decide to worship truly, we go all in, don't we?
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: They choose a new cart, fitting for the holiest burden. Abinadab's sons drive it—a family entrusted with care. Yet a cart is not the Lord's design; what seems reverent isn't always obedient. That's a hard lesson coming.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Ahio walks before the ark, leading the way with the holy thing. There's order here, ceremony. But the Lord's dwelling place is not carried safely by carts or processional decorum alone—He requires what His Word has already ordained.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Harps, tambourines, cymbals—all manner of music! David and Israel pour out joy before the Lord with every instrument they have. I've always loved that: the fullness of worship, bodies and voices rising together. Praise has never been a quiet thing.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: At Nacon's threshing floor, the cattle stumble. Uzzah sees the ark tip, and his hand shoots out to steady it. He means well—how could he not?—but good intention isn't the same as obedience to the Lord's boundary.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Lord's anger burns, and Uzzah falls dead on the spot. It seems harsh to our ears—a man trying to help? But the Lord guards His holiness fiercely. Not out of anger that destroys, but out of holiness that cannot be touched carelessly. There is a difference, though both hurt.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David names the place Perez Uzzah—'breaking out against Uzzah'—a name that would echo through generations. The Lord's mercy and the Lord's justice are both real, and both worthy of being remembered, not forgotten.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David's joy turns to fear. 'How could Yahweh's ark come to me?' The presence of the holy God does that to us—it breaks through our plans and our pride. Sometimes we need to be reminded that worship isn't a project we manage; it's a meeting with One far greater than ourselves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David doesn't bring the ark into the city after all. Instead, he sets it aside in Obed-Edom's house. It's not cowardice—it's wisdom learned through sorrow. Sometimes the godliest thing we do is step back and let the Lord teach us a different way.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Three months, the ark rests in Obed-Edom's care, and Yahweh blesses him and all his house. See how the Lord's presence brings blessing to those who reverence it? Even in waiting, even in sorrow, His favor falls on those who obey.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Word reaches David: the Lord has blessed Obed-Edom because of the ark. And now David's heart returns—with joy this time, not presumption. He's learned. The delay, the sorrow, the humbling—they've prepared him to bring the ark rightly into his city.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: After six paces, David stops and offers ox and calf—sacrifice marking the Lord's care. Each step forward is consecrated, not rushed. When we finally understand the weight of the holy, our feet learn to move with reverence.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David dances before Yahweh with all his might, clothed in a linen ephod—the garment of a priest. His whole body is worship. Joy and humility meet in the dance of a man who knows he's been forgiven and welcomed home by the God he serves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Shouting and trumpet sound—the joy of Israel is complete now. There's a fullness to this entry that the rushed, mistaken beginning lacked. The Lord's people, His king, His ark, His dwelling—all coming together in triumph and praise.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Michal watches from her window—the daughter of Saul, a woman who knows what it means to be displaced, to watch others rejoice while you hold your loss. She sees David leaping in joy, and something in her hardens. Pride can hide in judgment so easily.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The ark is set in the middle of the tent David has pitched. It is home now, in the City of David, surrounded by sacrifice and worship. The homeless sacred object has finally found its resting place with the Lord's anointed king.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David blesses the people in Yahweh's name—the king as priest, standing between heaven and earth. There's a tenderness in that: the Lord lets a repentant, renewed man speak His blessing to his people.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Bread, dates, raisins—portions to all, men and women alike. David's generosity spans the whole throng. Worship complete, the people go home nourished, reminded that the king who loves the Lord also loves them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Michal meets David with contempt veiled as concern. 'How glorious'—but her tone cuts. She mocks his dancing, his joy, calling him shameless. Sometimes those nearest us don't understand why we worship the way we do; sometimes they can't bear to see us love what they've rejected.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David stands firm: he dances before the Lord, not for the eyes of men. The Lord chose him over her father's house—a throne, a calling, a love. His worship is not for Michal's approval; it flows from a covenant with the King of Kings.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David will be even more vile, even more lowly, before the Lord. He's learned the freedom of complete submission—no vanity, no hiding. The servants will honor him because he has learned to honor the Lord above all. That's the way of the kingdom.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Michal had no children. She who scorned David's worship, who refused to join the joy—the line ends with her. It's a quiet note of sorrow, not triumph. Sometimes when we turn away from the Lord's joy, we find ourselves alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
